name: fortrip

tools.name: search_hotels
tools.description: Use this when the user wants hotels in a place they name, or a hotel by its name or brand. It finds hotels by destination and/or text, with an indicative per-room-night price when a stay is given. destination is the place the user asked for, never a location they did not give: a place_name with its countryCode, a place or locality by placeId from an earlier answer, a point (a landmark or an address the user named, or the coordinates hotel details showed), or a country. text matches hotel names, brands and areas word for word. Indicative prices are estimates and not bookable: get_hotel_offers returns what the user pays. A name several places bear answers destination_ambiguous, and a search too broad to price answers search_too_broad with its localities; each error says what to do next. The answer states what was searched, the counts and notes; a next page is the cursor and, optionally, limit.

destination.description: Where to search. A first page needs this or `text`.

kind.description: A place named in words, with its country.

name.description: The place name, in any language, e.g. Tokyo or 东京.

countryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the place is in, e.g. JP.

radiusMeters.description: Search radius around the destination in meters, 1 to 80000. Left out, the service picks one.

kind.description: A place id from an earlier response.

radiusMeters.description: Search radius around the destination in meters, 1 to 80000. Left out, the service picks one.

kind.description: A point the user asked to stay near: a landmark or an address they named, or the coordinates hotel details showed. Never a position the user did not give.

radiusMeters.description: Search radius around the destination in meters, 1 to 80000. Left out, the service picks one.

kind.description: A locality listed in an earlier search response.

radiusMeters.description: Search radius around the destination in meters, 1 to 80000. Left out, the service picks one.

text.description: Hotel name, brand or area to match, 1 to 128 characters. A first page needs this or `destination`.

stay.description: Dates and party. Needed for indicative prices. Search uses only the dates when the rooms differ.

checkIn.description: Check-in date in the hotel's calendar, yyyy-MM-dd.

checkOut.description: Check-out date in the hotel's calendar, yyyy-MM-dd. Stays are 1 to 15 nights; a longer one answers stay_unsupported (max_nights), and past 30 nights invalid_request: ask the user whether to split it into consecutive stays.

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in this room, 0 to 17. An empty list means no children.

rooms.description: The rooms wanted, 1 to 8, each with its party; offers and orders need every room the same.

pricing.description: `indicative` adds an indicative price per hotel and needs a stay; `none` skips prices. Default: indicative with a stay, otherwise none.

filters.description: Filters every hotel in the answer must pass.

stars.description: Star rating range. Unrated hotels are left out whenever it is set.

min.description: Lowest star rating, 1 to 5 in steps of 0.5.

max.description: Highest star rating, 1 to 5 in steps of 0.5.

amenities.description: Amenities every hotel must list, 1 to 9 of the codes a search can filter by. A hotel's own amenities can hold other codes.

price.description: Price limit. Needs indicative pricing, so a stay.

amount.description: Decimal string such as 132.40, never a number.

maxPerRoomNight.description: Highest price per room per night, in the search's currency.

sort.description: Result order. `distance` needs a destination, `relevance` needs `text`, `price_asc` and `price_desc` need indicative pricing. Default: relevance with `text`, otherwise distance.

cursor.description: The cursor the previous response gave for its next page (`nextCursor`). A next page is the cursor and, optionally, `limit`; nothing else.

locale.description: Language for names and text in the response: en or zh.

currency.description: The currency of every price: USD (default) or CNY. Each currency is paid through its own channel, with its own payment methods; the order's payment page shows them. CNY is paid through payment channels in mainland China and suits a user who pays that way.

tools.name: get_hotel
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about one hotel itself: where it is, its check-in and check-out times, its policies, amenities or room types. It returns the hotel's catalogue facts: names, address, coordinates, time zone, check-in and check-out times, the full description, every policy and the amenities, and its room types with include: "roomTypes". "Not listed" is not "no". No prices or availability: get_hotel_offers has those.

locale.description: Language for names and text in the response: en or zh.

tools.name: get_hotel_offers
tools.description: Use this when the user wants what a stay really costs or whether it can be booked, at hotels already found, and before create_order. It returns live, bookable offers for up to 15 hotels and one stay. Every room in stay.rooms must have the same party: for different parties, call once per party. Each offer has the room type, the meals included, the total, in the request's currency, for the whole stay and every room (what is charged), with its average per room-night for comparison, fees payable at the property, the cancellation terms with times in UTC and the hotel's time zone, the confirmation mode, and an offerId for create_order with the time it expires. Hotels with nothing to offer are listed as unavailable with the reason. Up to limitPerHotel offers per hotel (default 15, fewer when the call's hotels share its 45 offers), picked to span price, free cancellation, breakfast and rooms, listed cheapest first; the answer says, per hotel, how many more a call for that hotel alone would show.

hotelIds.description: Hotels to price, 1 to 15, no repeats.

checkIn.description: Check-in date in the hotel's calendar, yyyy-MM-dd.

checkOut.description: Check-out date in the hotel's calendar, yyyy-MM-dd. Stays are 1 to 15 nights; a longer one answers stay_unsupported (max_nights), and past 30 nights invalid_request: ask the user whether to split it into consecutive stays.

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in this room, 0 to 17. An empty list means no children.

rooms.description: The rooms wanted, 1 to 8, each with its party; offers and orders need every room the same.

stay.description: Dates and party. One party per call: every room must be the same.

requireBreakfast.description: Keep only offers that include breakfast.

requireFreeCancellation.description: Keep only offers that can still be cancelled free of charge.

limitPerHotel.description: Offers per hotel, 1 to 30. Left out: 15 for each hotel that has offers while that is at most 45 offers in all, otherwise 45 split evenly among those hotels (5 hotels: 9 each; 15 hotels: 3 each). Given: that many for each hotel while that is at most 100 offers in all, otherwise 100 split evenly the same way. The answer says, for each hotel, how many more offers a call for that hotel alone would show.

locale.description: Language for names and text in the response: en or zh.

currency.description: The currency of every price: USD (default) or CNY. Each currency is paid through its own channel, with its own payment methods; the order's payment page shows them. CNY is paid through payment channels in mainland China and suits a user who pays that way. An order made from these offers is charged in this currency.

tools.name: create_order
tools.description: Create an unpaid order when the user asks to book one offer from get_hotel_offers. It takes items, one item with the offer's offerId inside it (nowhere else in the arguments) and hotel.rooms, and contact. The answer is the order, awaiting payment: its reference, the total, the stay and its terms, and a payment link, a Fortrip page to pay on. Nothing is charged until the order is paid, on that page or with pay_order; anyone holding the link can pay. Send the contact and, for each room of the offer, at least one guest. If the price or terms changed since the offer, the answer is offer_changed with every change and a new offer: show the changes and ask the user again before ordering it. Sending the same details again returns the same order. An offer is ordered once: another order of the stay (another party, or a corrected guest name or contact) takes a new offer. cancel_order cancels or closes an order; for changes, or a cancellation it can't make, the user emails support@fortrip.ai with the order's reference.

offerId.description: The offer to order: an offerId from an offers response. It goes here, inside the item, and nowhere else in the request.

firstName.description: Guest's first name, in Latin letters as on the passport; transliterate accents (Müller → Mueller).

lastName.description: Guest's last name, in Latin letters as on the passport.

guests.description: Guests staying in this room: at least one, no more than the room sleeps. List only the guests the user named; one is enough, even when more adults share the room.

rooms.description: One entry per room of the offer, in order: as many entries as the offer has rooms, not one per adult.

specialRequests.description: Requests for the hotel, in English. Not guaranteed.

hotel.description: What the hotel needs to know.

items.description: What to order: exactly one item, which holds the offer's offerId and what its hotel needs to know. The offerId goes inside the item, not beside items.

name.description: Contact person's full name, in any script, at most 119 characters.

email.description: Contact email; the confirmation is sent here.

phone.description: Contact phone number, with country code.

contact.description: Who the hotel and the confirmation reach.

tools.name: get_order
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about one order of theirs: whether it is paid or confirmed, its terms, or what cancelling it would cost. It returns the order by orderId: its status, the payment status and, while it awaits payment, its payment link; the stay, its guests and its terms; whether it can be cancelled now, for which penalty and refund, or closed; why a failed order booked nothing and what a cancellation kept; and the hotel's confirmation number once there is one. It shows whether a payment went through.

locale.description: Language for names and text in the response: en or zh.

tools.name: list_orders
tools.description: Use this when the user asks what they have booked, or about an order whose orderId you do not have. It returns the user's hotel orders, newest first, including those made on the Fortrip website, each as get_order shows it. A next page is the cursor the answer gives.

cursor.description: The cursor the previous page of orders gave for the next one (`nextCursor`).

locale.description: Language for names and text in the response: en or zh.

tools.name: cancel_order
tools.description: Use this when the user asks to cancel a paid order or to close an unpaid one. It cancels a paid order under its terms, or closes an unpaid one. It takes the orderId and exactly one of maximumPenalty (a paid order) and close: true (an unpaid one). Paid (the order's Cancel line says it can be cancelled): pass maximumPenalty, the penalty on that line exactly as shown. The order becomes cancelling, then cancelled with the refund on its way, or confirmed again if the hotel refuses. If the penalty rose above maximumPenalty, the answer is cancellation_changed and nothing changed. Unpaid (the Cancel line says it can be closed): close: true closes it: nothing is charged, and it can no longer be paid. A mode that does not fit the order (close on an order paid meanwhile) answers order_not_cancellable, which says which mode applies now or what blocks both: nothing is cancelled or closed by the other mode. While a payment is under way the answer is payment_in_progress. The same call again answers the order as it is.

orderId.description: The orderId of the order to cancel.

close.description: Send true to close an unpaid order: nothing is charged. Send exactly one of close and maximumPenalty.

maximumPenalty.description: Send it to cancel a paid order: the penalty the user agreed to, as a ceiling. It is the penalty the order says a cancellation now keeps, exactly as the order gives it (cancel.penalty). Send exactly one of close and maximumPenalty.

amount.description: Decimal string such as 132.40, never a number.

tools.name: pay_order
tools.description: Pay a USD order without its payment link, with a Stripe shared payment token: for an agent that can request one from the user's Link wallet (US and Canadian accounts), and for an order whose text has a "Pay without the link" line, which gives the business_profile and the usage limits to request the token with. Any other order is paid by its link. It takes the orderId, the token as sharedPaymentToken and the order's total; a token pays one order. On success the order is confirming with its payment held, and its payment link stops working; a failure leaves the link open, and each error says how to recover.

orderId.description: The orderId of the order to pay.

sharedPaymentToken.description: The shared payment token (spt_…) the user approved for this order, requested with the usage limits the order gives for a token (payment.tokenRequest.usageLimits).

amount.description: Decimal string such as 132.40, never a number.

total.description: The total the user approved: the order's total, amount and currency, exactly as the order gives it (total). In USD: a token pays a USD order only, and any other order is paid by its payment link.

instructions:
Fortrip: hotel search, live offers and orders with a payment link.

Call order: `search_hotels` → (optional) `get_hotel` → `get_hotel_offers` → `create_order`; after the user pays, `get_order`; `list_orders` lists, `cancel_order` cancels a paid order or closes an unpaid one, `pay_order` pays by token. Every result is text: follow the rules that end it.

Sign-in happens only in the browser. Never ask the user to paste a token.
If a tool says the user isn't signed in, ask them to reconnect.

- A place name needs its `countryCode` (ask the user if unclear) and matches exactly (accents and periods count). On `destination_ambiguous`, ask the user which they mean, then search that place by its id; never pick one yourself.
- On `search_too_broad`, show its localities and ask the user which, unless they already named one; search it as `{ kind: "locality", placeId }`, never by name.
- `text` matches whole words of hotel names and addresses: use a distinctive name, brand or landmark.

- An order is in the currency of the offer it was made from. On a USD order, Stripe's page may let the user pay in their card's local currency at Stripe's rate.

- "Not listed" or "unknown" is not "no".

- Call `create_order` only for the offer the user picked, with at least one guest per room; never invent guests.
- `create_order` can take about two minutes. If it times out, call it again with the same details: it returns the same order.

- Pay one way only: give the payment link or call `pay_order`. First show the order's total and currency, the stay with each room's guests, the contact, any special requests and every term, end that reply by asking the user to confirm, and wait for a clear yes. Then give the payment link exactly as shown, to this user only: anyone holding it can pay.
- Another order of the stay (another party, a corrected name or contact) takes a new offer; when it replaces an unpaid order, tell the user to pay only the new link.
- Never ask for, accept or pass on payment card details; payment happens only on the payment link or, by token, through `pay_order`.

Cancel a paid order only after the user confirmed the penalty and the refund on its Cancel line; close an unpaid one only once they say they no longer want it. An order can't be changed, only cancelled under its terms and ordered again. For a cancellation that `cancel_order` can't make, or other problems, the user emails support@fortrip.ai with the order's reference (never its payment link).
